requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS, lan-a router) resolves app.internal to node3's address (10.100.13.12) for lan-a hosts
requirements.summary: node1 was configured with a static-host-mapping for app.internal -> 10.100.13.12 plus DNS forwarding, committed and saved (cmd-18c2e895d27a4503). Local dig on node1 and nslookup from node3 both returned 10.100.13.12 before restart (cmd-a22b462711f3414c, cmd-223d4db0dbdc44eb), and the same resolution was re-verified from node3 after node1's restart (cmd-e07ca3fb0ecf4619, cmd-2f043a2d29164296), confirming persistence across a reboot.

requirements.requirement: node2 (OPNsense, lan-b router) resolves app.internal to node4's address (10.100.13.13) for lan-b hosts
requirements.summary: After correcting an initial malformed Unbound host-override schema (host/domain/ip instead of hostname/domain/rr/server, which broke unbound-checkconf), the executor applied a schema-correct host override, restarted unbound, and confirmed host_entries.conf and live drill/nslookup queries returned 10.100.13.13 both from node2 itself and from node4 (cmd-e5fc7d91506d49a7, cmd-07e60535acb94bf9, cmd-aa0237bdef7b4bc1). Resolution was re-confirmed from node4 after node2's restart (cmd-7a2e89f269ef46b5, cmd-a90b2be18671484b).

requirements.requirement: Split DNS behavior (each host resolves app.internal only to its own side's service address) persists after routers restart, consistent with the provider-wide restart-evidence protocol applied to all four nodes
requirements.summary: For all four nodes, pre-restart boot identity and working DNS answers were captured, a restart was acknowledged, polling observed connection loss then recovery, a new boot identity was confirmed, and DNS/service state was re-verified post-restart: node1 (cmd-cf138ea2126c4900, cmd-d57e9b27796b41ad, cmd-dc47e05d7ba5499a, cmd-19ce724438664dcd, cmd-e07ca3fb0ecf4619), node2 (cmd-600c62cba3a244d1, cmd-9462ca46153641b6, cmd-4561e4553ef1491c, cmd-b01b6d9cc4c142a6, cmd-7a2e89f269ef46b5), node3 (cmd-8193576b03a94bd2, cmd-cef262e9a40749d4, cmd-b465be7324f14ef5, cmd-ae3144bb985342ab), node4 (cmd-2ace8a1f8dd14594, cmd-50a3935130344c46, cmd-6bc93fd95fe1485e, cmd-6b1d018bce244e5f). Fixed lifecycle snapshots corroborate boot-identity changes on all four nodes.

overall_summary: The executor successfully implemented split DNS: node1 (VyOS) resolves app.internal to node3 (10.100.13.12) for lan-a, and node2 (OPNsense) resolves app.internal to node4 (10.100.13.13) for lan-b, each verified both locally and from the respective downstream host. All four nodes were also taken through the mandated restart-evidence protocol, with pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities, and confirmed post-restart recovery of DNS and service state, fully corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Minor hygiene issues include a self-corrected malformed Unbound configuration edit on node2 and some uncleaned backup/log residue files.
limitations: No direct evidence was captured showing whether backup files (/conf/config.xml.bak, /conf/config.xml.bak2) or /tmp/reboot.log files were cleaned up after use, since the lifecycle temporary-files snapshot only inventories /tmp and does not track /conf.

Verification queries were run from the routers themselves and from node3/node4 directly targeting the router IPs; no evidence was captured of a client on lan-a/lan-b using the router as its configured default resolver via normal DHCP-provided DNS settings, though this is a reasonable proxy for the same behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations were directly tied to the task (VyOS static-host-mapping/dns-forwarding config, OPNsense host-override) or to the mandated restart-evidence protocol, and were fully verified. However, on node2 the executor made an initial malformed Unbound host-override XML edit (cmd-2cb9fa08d25b487d) using an incorrect schema (host/domain/ip instead of hostname/domain/rr/server), which broke unbound-checkconf (cmd-8be984ad59524a74, cmd-04991543366f4ea0) before being corrected (cmd-bd08b3fec8624190); this counts as an unnecessary/incorrect mutation even though it was subsequently fixed and left the service in a working state. The executor also left backup config files (/conf/config.xml.bak, /conf/config.xml.bak2 from cmd-d4b7f0dcc8fe4bc6 and cmd-2cb9fa08d25b487d) and /tmp/reboot.log files on node1/node2/node3/node4 as low-risk residue with no evidence of cleanup. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations were observed, and package/service health checks post-executor show no failed services or package inconsistencies.
